diffs.diff: chip ID register 0x7: part 33236, datasheet reading 54401
diffs.evidence: Both values describe the same register. The difference is only in how the bytes are encoded. Vishay VEML6030 datasheet (doc 84366), Command Code #7: 'The low byte of the ID register contains the device specific ID code 81h. The high byte contains a code that depends on the chosen slave address option: either 0xC4 for a device with slave address 0x20, or 0xD4 for a device with slave address 0x90'. Table 8 gives bits 15:8 = 0xD4 for option 0x90 and bits 7:0 = 0x81. 0x90 is the 8-bit write address of 7-bit address 0x48, the SparkFun default, so the logical 16-bit value is 0xD481 = 54401. The read protocol in the same datasheet is 'S, Slave address, Wr, A, Command code, A, S, Slave address, Rd, A, Data byte (LSB), A, Data byte (MSB), N, P', so the bytes on the wire are 0x81 then 0xD4. The simulator's 16-bit register store (src/sim/devices.ts setReg: [(v >> 8) & 0xff, v & 0xff]) always sends the high byte of the stored value first and has no little-endian option for static registers. Storing 0x81D4 = 33236 is therefore what makes it send 0x81 then 0xD4. The 0x00 entry follows the same rule: 256 = 0x0100 sends 0x01, 0x00, which is the datasheet power-on default 'Command code 0 default value is 01 = devices is shut down'. The driver reads d[0] | (d[1] << 8), which gives 0xD481, and checks that the low byte is 0x81. SKILL.md says 'low byte 0x81; high byte 0xD4 at 0x48, 0xC4 at 0x10'. The model's value is the correct wire-order encoding of the datasheet ID, and no change is needed. This is the same convention already accepted for the VEML7700 part (33220 = 0x81C4).
